column1: Incorporating the Beige Book around May 2018 slightly brightens the tone versus the FOMC statement alone. Districts reported modest-to-moderate growth broadly, very tight labor markets with modest-to-moderate wage gains, and generally upbeat business sentiment. Manufacturing and freight were strong; consumer spending was mixed (notably softer autos), and residential construction was constrained by labor and materials. Price pressures were moderate but building, with rising input costs (e.g., steel/aluminum) and trade policy uncertainty flagged as headwinds. Credit demand was steady to modestly higher, with standards largely unchanged but somewhat tighter in CRE and parts of consumer credit—consistent with SLOOS nuances showing easier C&I terms and firmer business loan demand. Net: near-term conditions look a bit firmer than the statement implies, though medium‑term risks from cost pressures, trade uncertainty, and risk‑taking persist. Adjusting for the Beige Book, I nudge the assessment modestly higher. sentiment score = 0.58
